rows.grounds: direct object of the imperative; refers to the supreme nectar mentioned in context
compound qualifying the nectar as the authentic reality of Kaula
imperative address instructing the listener to attend to the teaching
compound qualifying the nectar as having the nature of kāmakalā

items.question: What essential nature characterizes the Kaula nectar that must be heard?
premises: A nectar is presented as the object to be heard.
This nectar is identified as the true essence of Kaula.
This nectar is characterized as having the nature of kāmakalā.
items.inference: The Kaula nectar to be heard is the true Kaula essence whose nature is kāmakalā.
uncertainties: The precise doctrinal nuance of kāmakalā in this context is not fully specified within the verse alone.
items.plain_english: Hear of the nectar, the true essence of Kaula, whose nature is kāmakalā.
